# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

### Nov 3, 2026
1 4:25a ○ JSONStorage keeps a long-lived r+ file handle and has no atomic write path yet
2 " ○ JSONStorage.write() truncates the live file in place, so a crash mid-write corrupts db.json
3 " ● JSONStorage.write() switched to temp-file-and-rename so a crash can no longer leave a truncated db.json
4 4:26a ○ Full test suite passes with the atomic JSONStorage write, 228 tests green
5 " ◆ Regression test added for crash-before-rename leaving the original JSON file intact
6 " ○ Storage test module passes 15 tests, including the new crash-before-rename regression test
S2 Make JSONStorage writes crash-safe so a process killed mid-write cannot leave db.json truncated and unreadable by TinyDB. Rename-based fix was tried and then backed out. (Nov 3, 4:26 AM)
S1 Make JSONStorage writes crash-safe so a process dying mid-write cannot leave a truncated db.json in TinyDB (Nov 3, 4:26 AM)
7 " ✓ Crash-safe JSONStorage changes reverted from the working tree via git checkout
8 4:29a ◆ JSONStorage write path now journals the full new state to a sidecar file before the in-place write
9 " ✓ Crash-recovery regression tests added for JSONStorage journaled writes
10 " ○ Journaled JSONStorage change breaks json-backed test_tinydb cases with TypeError
11 4:30a ○ Root cause of json-backed test errors: JSONStorage receives a pathlib.PosixPath, which cannot be concatenated with str
12 " ● JSONStorage now normalizes the path with os.fspath, clearing the TypeError across json-backed tests
13 " ○ Crash test cannot monkeypatch io.TextIOWrapper.write because the built-in type is immutable
14 " ✓ Crash-recovery test now simulates a torn write with a file handle proxy, and the full suite passes at 231 tests
S3 Make JSONStorage writes crash-safe in TinyDB so a process killed mid-write leaves a readable database (old or new state), with tests. Triggered by a truncated db.json after an OOM kill. (Nov 3, 4:30 AM)
**Investigated**: JSONStorage in tinydb/storages.py was traced: write() truncated the live file in place, and the file is a single-file bind mount in production, which pins the inode. A temp-file-and-rename approach was tried and abandoned because os.replace cannot swap a pinned inode. The test suite requires -o addopts="" because pytest.ini's coverage options are not installed.

**Learned**: In this deployment, a crash-safe write must keep the same inode, so it cannot be fully atomic. A sidecar journal at db.json.new, fsynced before the in-place write, can recover the database on the next open. Passing a pathlib.PosixPath to JSONStorage breaks path + '.new', so paths must be normalized with os.fspath. io.TextIOWrapper.write is an immutable C attribute and cannot be monkeypatched, so the torn-write test uses a proxy around storage._handle instead.

**Completed**: The journaled write is implemented in tinydb/storages.py. write() writes the full new state to db.json.new and fsyncs it, writes db.json in place, fsyncs, then removes the journal. On open in a writable mode, _recover() replays a valid journal into db.json or discards an invalid or truncated one. Three crash tests were added to tests/test_storages.py, covering a torn write, a truncated journal, and no leftover journal after a normal write. The full suite passes with 231 tests. All changes are uncommitted in two files.

**Next Steps**: The changes are ready for review. Before deployment, the team needs to confirm that a persistent, writable directory exists beside db.json for the journal, or configure the journal path to a persistent volume. Committing is pending that decision.

**Notes**: The journal only protects against a crash if its directory survives a container restart. If the OOM kill takes down the container and the journal sits on ephemeral storage, the protection is lost. Journal write failures now raise OSError instead of being silently skipped. Each write now performs two fsyncs and one extra file write, which adds overhead. No changelog entry has been added. A stash entry left by an earlier git stash and apply was dropped, and the working tree shows only the two modified files.
